Mechanical half of #208's recommendation. #208 landed the convention (`docs/agents/handoff.md`) and the arithmetic (`docs/research/continuation-economics.md`) at `ae79d12`; this is the retrieval tool that makes it cheap to consume.

## Why

#208 measured that **85.6% of a subagent's first-ten-turn state reconstruction is GitHub-thread reading** — `gh issue view` alone is 53.8% of it. That is the reason the handoff goes in an issue comment: a continuation is already looking there. But it is also the reason the retrieval needs a tool. `gh issue view --comments` on a long thread returns the whole thread, and everything a successor reads on turn 1 is billed **12.55×** over a median 114-turn agent's life. Fetching a 1,500-character handoff by reading a 40,000-character thread defeats the point.

## What

A `just handoff <issue>` recipe that prints the **most recent** comment on the issue whose body contains a `Handoff-for:` line, and nothing else. Suggested shape (the `--jq` does the filtering server-side-ish, so the thread never reaches context):

    gh api repos/andrewesweet/arma-cti/issues/<n>/comments --paginate \
      --jq '[.[] | select(.body | test("^Handoff-for:"; "m"))] | last | .body'

Requirements:

- **Exit non-zero with a clear message when there is no handoff comment**, rather than printing nothing. A silent empty result reads as "no state to carry" when it may mean "wrong issue number" — the #168/#183 fail-open lesson in a new place.
- **Print only the matched comment body.** No thread, no metadata beyond what the handoff itself carries.
- Consider a companion `just handoff-write` or leave authoring manual — authoring is prose and a template already exists; do not build a form.

## The gated-row collision

The command surface table lives in CLAUDE.md, which is human-gated, so this recipe cannot land its own table row. That is exactly the collision #198/#199 hit; **ADR-0057's reconciliation clause applies** — propose the row in the close and let it follow through the gate rather than lag silently.

## Gate

No Arma surface. `just fast` is the gate. The `--jq` filter deserves a unit test against a fixture comment list (present, absent, several — last wins), in the no-Arma tier, per the #83 precedent that a classification bug should be a red `just unit` rather than a discovery.

Refs #208, #204
